# Maintained WebView binding

The Windows desktop uses the pinned `github.com/wailsapp/go-webview2` v1.0.23 source with explicit owned-window and callback lifetime corrections. Wails destroys its window without closing the controller. The added window subclass closes that controller once on its owning UI thread and preserves ordinary native destruction. A close error survives the remaining application cleanup and fails qualification.

The source manifest records every original file hash, the original Go module checksum, every maintained file hash and the maintained tree checksum. Only `pkg/combridge/iunknown.go`, `pkg/edge/ICoreWebView2Deferral.go`, `pkg/edge/ICoreWebView2WebResourceRequestedEventArgs.go`, `pkg/edge/ICoreWebView2WebResourceResponse.go`, `pkg/edge/chromium.go`, `pkg/edge/corewebview2.go` and `pkg/edge/create_env_go.go` change upstream bytes. The additions contain owned-window/callback lifetime implementations, unshown native regressions, the project license and an explicit patch notice. Original upstream license bytes remain intact.

Repository checks verify all source bytes, membership, the upstream `go.sum` binding, the declared replacement and the precise patch scope. Package notices independently rehash the maintained source before copying its notices. Go records this exact relative replacement without a module checksum, so the clean product source revision and the verified maintained-source manifest provide its source authority. Other local replacements remain rejected. Installed notice verification requires the explicit patch notice and both applicable licenses.

Updates require a reviewed change to the pinned upstream identity, source manifest and verifier allowlist. Product versions and existing immutable release records are independent of this source-maintenance record. Local SDK verification selects unshown native-vtable, ownership and message-only-window regressions; actual browser and product qualification runs on disposable CI.

The owned window closes its controller and releases its retained WebView/controller/environment references on its UI thread. The application balances the binding's existing COM apartment initialization after Wails returns (and on other normal desktop mode returns); cleanup refuses a different thread or still-owned windows. The original SDK already pins that initialization thread.

Resource deferral cleanup dispatches its Release method to IUnknown.Release. The selected unshown native regression checks one completion and balanced acquired references; it does not substitute for browser navigation acceptance.

The v1.0.23 upstream baseline corrects the monitor-scale Boolean argument during controller initialization. The production edge wrapper has an actual native-vtable regression for false/true and HRESULT propagation. The unused generated API is not part of the linked desktop and has no native execution qualification claim.

Disposable qualification observes the first native resource response through final content publication and deferral completion using bounded counters. It records actual entered/returned status, HRESULT and owning-thread relation without adding WebView2 COM calls. Those observations do not establish browser consumption; the existing runtime version field records availability rather than the created environment identity.

The nine active Chromium callbacks reuse the existing native-allocated COM bridge. It returns supported interfaces and canonical IUnknown identity, rejects unimplemented interfaces and retains Go targets until final native release. Creator leases begin after owned-window attachment and close after controller/interface cleanup. Never-embedded objects create no callback registry cycle. The default Go loader captures its completion target before scheduling, and late callbacks cannot install a controller or notify application code after shutdown.
